en: Morning dew on grass in Baguio forms when water vapor in the cool air condenses into liquid water.
Seawater in Manila Bay is a homogeneous mixture where salt is completely dissolved in liquid water.
The skin of a Guimaras mango changing from green to yellow is a chemical change.
Molten lava from Mayon Volcano is a liquid that cools and solidifies into hard basalt rock.
White sand in Boracay is a heterogeneous mixture containing visible pieces of crushed coral and quartz.
Water splashing from Pagsanjan Falls absorbs heat and undergoes a physical change to become water vapor.
Bubbles rising in a freshly opened bottle of local soda contain dissolved carbon dioxide gas.
Fallen narra leaves decomposing on the forest floor undergo a chemical change to become nutrient-rich soil.
Pure virgin coconut oil melts from a solid into a clear liquid at about twenty-four degrees Celsius.
Floodwater in Manila is a heterogeneous suspension where solid dirt particles temporarily float in liquid water.
Crushing porous pumice rocks collected near Taal Volcano is a physical change because the material remains solid.
Bamboo logs float down the Agusan River because the solid plant material is less dense than water.
